title: /audit:version says which build is running and whether a newer one is published
desiredOutcome: one command prints the running version, what the marketplace clone offers and whether it auto-updates, the installed copies, and the newest published release - each with its basis - and says exactly how to update

findings.issue: an installed version that does not parse defaulted to 0.0.0 and was called older than the running copy
findings.resolution: fixed in P67.3-2e7: said to be not comparable (v9e)

findings.issue: parse_version dropped a pre-release suffix, so 3.1.0-beta read as 3.1.0 and up to date

review.outcome: matches; two findings (one med, one low) fixed in P67.3-2e7

summary: A new command, /audit:version, reports which build of the plugin is running, what the marketplace it came from offers and whether that marketplace auto-updates, every installed copy by project, and the newest published GitHub release - each line naming where it was read, a source that could not be read saying why - and prints the documented update commands when a newer release is out. Versions compare as semver; an unanswered release feed is never reported as up to date. The release check is the plugin's one outbound request, stated in SECURITY.md and skipped by --offline. Desired outcome met, driven live against this machine's installed copies. Reviewed in phase mode (two findings, fixed); the phase gate ran green with the tree unchanged; the invariant check found no breach.

Prints each fact with its basis, a verdict, and the documented update commands.
